scope: Independent cross-review of Chapters1-2; no edits to authors content or shared files

issues.location: C1-Q1 reference answer, first explanation paragraph
issues.finding: The answer says capillarity and viscosity resist motion. Constant surface tension penalizes expansion and assists collapse; viscosity dissipates motion of either sign.
issues.proposed_fix: In both languages, say capillarity penalizes expansion while viscosity dissipates motion in either direction.
issues.basis: The capillary term is always negative in outward-positive RP. Its mechanical power is minus d(4 pi sigma R^2)/dt and can be positive during collapse.
issues.resolution: Parent applied the proposed bilingual qualification; reviewer verified the edited source. No author/shared files edited by reviewer.

issues.finding: The displayed s dot D n=0 divides out viscosity without stating mu>0. At mu=0 the tangential traction vanishes automatically and imposes no strain constraint.
issues.proposed_fix: Retain 2 mu s dot D n=0 as the traction condition, or restrict the divided form to mu>0; keep the inviscid closure free of this strain constraint.
issues.basis: Newtonian stress is minus p I plus 2 mu D. With constant clean surface tension and neglected gas shear, tangential traction is 2 mu s dot D n.
issues.resolution: Parent applied the proposed bilingual qualification; reviewer verified the edited source. No author/shared files edited by reviewer.

issues.location: Step 21 paragraph before the thermal product-rule display
issues.finding: The prose calls h_boundary minus e_bulk entirely flow work, while local definitions explicitly allow the boundary temperature to differ from the bulk temperature.
issues.proposed_fix: State that it is pure flow work only at the same thermodynamic state; otherwise include the boundary-to-bulk internal-energy difference. Translate the same qualification into Chinese.
issues.basis: h(Ti)-e(Tb)=[e(Ti)-e(Tb)]+p_boundary/rho_boundary. The equation is correct; only the interpretation needs qualification.
issues.resolution: Parent applied the proposed bilingual qualification; reviewer verified the edited source. No author/shared files edited by reviewer.

issues.location: Worked Stefan sign-control paragraph after C2-E21
issues.finding: The pure-component interface example labels rho_l=1000 as aqueous carrier density immediately within a PFC phase-change discussion. For PFC-to-vapor transfer, rho_l is adjacent PFC-liquid density, distinct from carrier density in RP inertia.
issues.proposed_fix: Either label 1000 a stipulated adjacent single-component liquid density for a separate mathematical sign-control, or use the PFC teaching density 1630 and slip 0.00613497 m/s. Keep mixture species transfer limitations explicit.
issues.basis: Mass jump flux equals rho_l (interface radial speed minus adjacent radial liquid speed). It uses the density of the actual liquid adjacent to that phase interface.
issues.resolution: Parent applied the proposed bilingual qualification; reviewer verified the edited source. No author/shared files edited by reviewer.
